headline: Why Does My Remodel Always Go Over Budget?
articleBody: It's a common headache: your remodeling budget seems to grow legs and run away! One big reason is not setting aside enough contingency funds from the start. We're talking 10-20% of your total project cost. Things happen during construction—unforeseen issues, a change of heart on a material—and having that buffer saves you from stress and financial strain. Another mistake is relying on vague, lump-sum quotes. It's tough to compare apples to apples when bids aren't itemized, leaving room for hidden costs to surface later. You want to see exactly what you're paying for. Verbal approvals for changes are also a big no-no. Always get change orders in writing, detailing new costs and schedule impacts. This keeps everyone on the same page and prevents nasty surprises. Finally, starting construction without a rock-solid written scope is like building on sand. If you don't know exactly what's included (and excluded!), it's easy for the project to expand, and with it, your budget. A detailed scope defines the boundaries, protecting your wallet. If you're tackling a big project, a professional like Frasheski Construction can help you manage these budget pitfalls right from the start.
